GRADING: a checker fails you for touching files outside the owned list, production code with no tests, fewer than 8 new def test_..., no negative test, or the verify command failing.

OWNED FILES (only these — create both):
  server/pipeline/loop_runner.py
  tests/test_loop_runner.py

DO NOT EDIT server/pipeline/orchestrator.py. Your module must be callable from it later without editing it now.

SOURCE OF TRUTH: docs/SPEC-autonomous-podcast-loop.md. Read it in the worktree first.

WHAT EXISTS. server/pipeline/loop_tick.plan_tick(world, now=...) is a PURE
function: given a world snapshot it returns {"queue", "actions", "escalations",
"skipped"}. It performs nothing. Read its real signature and return shape in the
worktree before writing code. Nothing currently assembles a world or executes a
plan, so the loop cannot run.

BUILD server/pipeline/loop_runner.py — two halves, kept separate so the risky
half stays small:

  assemble_world(episodes_dir, *, now, extra=None) -> dict
      Reads episode.json files under episodes_dir plus the publish calendar, and
      returns the world dict plan_tick expects. Read-only: it must not write or
      mutate anything on disk. An unreadable or malformed episode.json is SKIPPED
      and recorded in the returned world under "load_errors", never silently
      dropped and never fatal: one corrupt file must not blind the whole loop.

  execute_plan(plan, *, performers, dry_run=True, now) -> dict
      Executes the plan's actions in order. Returns {"performed": [...],
      "refused": [...], "failed": [...], "dry_run": bool}.
      NON-NEGOTIABLE RULES:
        * dry_run defaults to TRUE. A caller must opt in to real effects.
          Under dry_run nothing is performed; each action is recorded in
          "performed" with a "dry_run": true marker so a tick can be inspected
          safely.
        * Every action whose kind is an external effect is dispatched through
          server.pipeline.outbound.dispatch, never by calling a performer
          directly. The gateway is the only path to the outside world; bypassing
          it removes the kill switch, the ledger and idempotency in one step.
        * When dispatch returns a blocked or refused outcome, that goes in
          "refused" with the gateway's reason. A refusal is NEVER retried inside
          the same tick and NEVER converted into a failure that gets retried
          elsewhere.
        * An exception from any single action is caught, recorded in "failed"
          with the action id and the error, and execution CONTINUES with the
          remaining actions. One bad action must not abort the tick.
        * The function never raises for an individual action outcome. It raises
          only if the plan itself is structurally unusable.

  run_tick(episodes_dir, *, now, dry_run=True, performers=None) -> dict
      assemble_world, then plan_tick, then execute_plan. Returns a single record
      containing the queue status, the plan, the execution result, and a
      "summary" line a human can read. This is the function a cron entry point
      or the orchestrator will call.

  Never call datetime.now() inside these; take `now` and pass it through, so a
  tick is reproducible and testable.

TESTS (tests/test_loop_runner.py, tmp_path episode fixtures, mocked dispatch; at least 8):
 (1) assemble_world reads several episode.json files into the expected shape;
 (2) NEGATIVE: a corrupt episode.json is recorded in load_errors and the other
     episodes still load — one bad file does not blind the loop;
 (3) NEGATIVE: assemble_world writes nothing (assert file mtimes and directory
     listing are unchanged after the call);
 (4) THE DEFAULT: execute_plan with no dry_run argument performs NOTHING real
     and marks every entry dry_run true;
 (5) NEGATIVE: with dry_run False, every external action goes through
     outbound.dispatch (assert the mock was called) and no performer is invoked
     directly;
 (6) NEGATIVE: a dispatch returning blocked lands in "refused" with the reason
     and is not retried within the tick;
 (7) NEGATIVE: an action that raises is recorded in "failed" and the following
     actions still execute;
 (8) run_tick returns queue, plan, execution and a non-empty summary;
 (9) determinism: two run_tick calls with the same fixtures and same now
     produce the same plan.
tasks.verified: world assembled read-only, plan executed through the gateway only, dry-run by default, one bad action never aborts the tick

WHAT EXISTS. server/pipeline/loop_runner.run_tick(episodes_dir, now=..., dry_run=True, performers=None) assembles the world, plans the tick and executes it. Read its real signature in the worktree; another lane is writing it, so if it is absent, code against the signature above and note that in a comment. Nothing yet invokes it on a schedule.

BUILD scripts/run_loop_tick.py — the operator entry point:
  Argparse CLI:
    run_loop_tick.py [--episodes-dir PATH] [--live] [--json OUT] [--quiet]
  * DEFAULT IS DRY RUN. Real effects require the explicit --live flag. A missing
    flag must never be interpreted as live: this is the difference between
    inspecting a tick and sending email to real people.
  * Prints a human-readable summary: queue count and health, how many actions
    were planned, performed, refused and failed, and each escalation. A person
    reading the log must be able to tell what the loop decided and why without
    opening JSON.
  * Exit codes: 0 when the tick completed (even with refusals, which are normal
    and expected), 1 when the tick could not complete, 2 on unusable input such
    as a missing episodes directory.
  * --json writes the full record for machine consumption.
  * Never prints a guest's email address, a message body, or any secret.

BUILD the systemd unit and timer:
  * The service runs the script. Ship the timer with the same DISABLED-by-default
    convention already used in scripts/systemd (read podcast-publish-drain.timer
    in the worktree and match its header comment style and structure).
  * The service must NOT pass --live. Enabling autonomy is a deliberate,
    separate act by the owner, not a side effect of installing a timer.
  * Timer cadence: hourly is right for a loop whose fastest obligation is a
    weekly publish; a five-minute tick would add noise without adding safety.
    State the rationale in a comment.

TESTS (tests/test_loop_cli.py, subprocess or main() invocation with mocked
run_tick; at least 5):
 (1) THE DEFAULT: invoking with no flags calls run_tick with dry_run True;
 (2) NEGATIVE and central: --live is the ONLY way dry_run becomes False;
 (3) NEGATIVE: a missing episodes directory exits 2, not 0;
 (4) a tick containing refusals still exits 0, since refusal is normal;
 (5) NEGATIVE: the printed summary contains no email address when the tick
     record includes one (feed a record containing a plausible address and
     assert it is absent from stdout);
 (6) --json writes a parseable record;
 (7) the shipped timer file contains the disabled-by-default header and the
     service does not contain --live (assert by reading the unit files).
tasks.verified: operator entry point and a disabled-by-default timer; --live is the only path to real effects and the service never carries it
